description: issue #775 (review gate, QA finding B2): `every "0"` -- the RANGE arm of `every`'s tick count reached through a WORD, the twin of `wait/wait-negative-word`. `spec/interaction-events.md`'s `### every <n> <block>` requires a positive whole number and raises `ol-range` on a zero or negative one; `spec/execution-model.md:33-34` makes "words that parse as numbers are accepted where a number is expected" a normative CORE rule, so `"0"` MUST reach that `ol-range` exactly as the literal `0` does (pinned by the sibling `every-zero-range-error`). Nothing covered the composition of those two rules: every RANGE fixture passed a number literal, so an implementation that trusted the type check to have already handled words -- guarding the range only when the argument was literally a number -- would REGISTER a handler with an interval of 0, an unbounded-rerun hazard, and still pass a fully green run (found by mutation). Note `params.value` is the COERCED number `0`, not the word `"0"` -- the opposite of the `ol-type` arm (`every-non-whole-word`), and deliberately so: `ol-range` is a question about magnitude, which only exists after coercion, while `ol-type` is a question about what the learner actually wrote. The check fails BEFORE registration, so no `primitive` event is emitted and no handler is registered; only the registration instruction precedes the diagnostic, and the span covers just the count argument.
